# Warlock Grimoire — full skills

> Package: `@warlock.js/grimoire`

> Generated artifact. Concatenates every SKILL.md and reference file under `@warlock.js/grimoire/skills/`. Re-run `node scripts/generate-llms.mjs` after any change.

## Package orientation

---
description: "Grimoire (experimental), the project map for Warlock.js apps: `warlock scry` and `warlock grimoire build|check|release` over a `grimoire/` folder of generated book entries and agent-written features, flows, apps, tasks and releases. Topics: use the map before searching code, write a feature, record a change and release, describe sites and mobile screens, document a file, backfill an existing app. Use at the start of every task in a project that has `grimoire/`."
---

# @warlock.js/grimoire

The Grimoire is experimental: its file structure and commands may still change.

`grimoire/` is the map of a Warlock.js project. Warlock writes the **book** (one entry per source file, the routes, the pages and the mobile screens, in `grimoire/book/`, not in git). Agents write what the product does (`grimoire/features/`), where users meet it (`grimoire/apps/`), the work (`grimoire/tasks/`) and the releases (`grimoire/releases/`). Warlock never edits a file an agent wrote, apart from the changelog stamp you ask for with `warlock grimoire release --stamp`.

## The 80% path

1. Before searching the code, ask the map: `use-the-grimoire.md`.
2. A new behaviour starts as a task, a brief, a feature README and a flow, before code: `write-a-feature.md`.
3. After the change, tie tests to criteria (`@proves`, and `@shows` for what the user sees), reshape the README, add the changelog entry, close the task, run the check, and at release time stamp the changelogs and write the brief: `record-a-change.md`.
4. Pages, blocks, conditions and mobile screens: `describe-an-app.md`.
5. The header and export comments the book copies from a file: `document-a-file.md`.
6. A project with code but no `grimoire/` folder: `backfill-a-grimoire.md`.
7. Keep a change inside its task (features, `Files:`, locked tests, protected areas) and run `warlock grimoire guard` before you stop: `guard-a-change.md`.
8. Review a change from its task and its diff only, never from the author's summary: `review-a-change.md`.

## Conventions and pitfalls

- Never edit `grimoire/book/`, `index.json`, `bookmap.json` or `*.bookmap.json`.
- `warlock grimoire release <version> --stamp` moves every `## Unreleased` entry under the release and writes a missing release file; without `--stamp` it only writes the collected list.
- Every project has a design-system feature first (`grimoire/features/design-system/`); flows with a page step name it in `affects`.
- Only the owner approves a changed screenshot or a removed criterion (`warlock grimoire approve`); list every change that is not approved in your report.
- A finding marked `(expected)` belongs to `proposed` work and does not fail `warlock grimoire check`.
- Mobile screens are listed from file names only with file-based routing; declare them when navigation is in code.
- Do not invent intent: write `Unknown:` and ask the owner.


## backfill-a-grimoire  `@warlock.js/grimoire/skills/backfill-a-grimoire/SKILL.md`

---
name: backfill-a-grimoire
description: "Write the Grimoire for a project that already has code but no `grimoire/` folder: build the book, propose features from the modules and routes, write them as inferred, and bring the owner the questions only they can answer. Use once per existing project, or when a large undescribed area is found."
---

# Backfill a Grimoire

The Grimoire is experimental: its file structure and commands may still change.

The code exists; the description does not. You will infer intent from code, and inference can be
plausible and wrong. So everything you write here is marked **inferred** until the owner confirms
it, and you bring them questions instead of guessing.

## 1. Build the book

```bash
npx warlock grimoire build
```

It needs no writing. Read the module summaries (`grimoire/book/app/<module>/index.md`), the
route list (`grimoire/book/app/routes.json`) and each site's page list.

## 2. Propose the features

Start from the modules: a module is usually one feature. Then adjust.

- Two modules that cannot be described without each other → one feature with both `folders`.
- A module that does two unrelated things → two features; tag the files of the smaller one.
- A folder shared by several features (a `components` folder with files of each) → list the files
  each feature owns in its `folders`, one entry per file (`folders: [src/app/auth, src/web/components/login-form.tsx]`),
  instead of tagging them in the code. A file entry wins over a folder of another feature.
- Plumbing (config, shared utilities, the base layout) → no feature.
- Mail, notifications, search: the machinery is a feature; each mail or notification belongs to
  the feature that sends it.

In a project with a UI, write the `design-system` feature first (`write-a-feature`), as `inferred`:
direction, components, error messages. Add `grimoire/settings.md` with the app's `languages`; the
Warlock adapter would read `app.localeCodes` anyway, but the file makes the choice visible.

Write the proposal as a table for the owner **before** writing files:

| Feature | Folders      | Flows you see                  | Apps               | Unsure about               |
| ------- | ------------ | ------------------------------ | ------------------ | -------------------------- |
| auth    | src/app/auth | sign-up, login, reset-password | web-client, mobile | is phone login still used? |

Wait for the owner's answer on the list. Features are the frame for everything else; a wrong
frame costs the most to fix.

## 3. Write each feature as inferred

Follow `write-a-feature` for the shapes, with these differences:

```md
---
id: auth
title: Accounts
status: shipped
origin: inferred
version: 1.0
updated: 2026-11-16
apps: [web-client, mobile]
folders: [src/app/auth]
---
```

- `origin: inferred` on the README and on each flow. The owner changes it to `confirmed`.
- **Summaries and stories in plain words.** Write the paragraph under each flow's title (what a user
  does and gets, in one or two sentences) and, where the route and page names make the path clear,
  a `## Story` of numbered sentences in the user's words. Add `audience` and a short `## Why` to
  the README when the code shows who uses the feature and for what. Mark all of it inferred and
  leave a screenshot out unless you can capture it; the owner confirms the wording.
- Start every feature at `1.0`. Do not reconstruct history; the changelog gets one line under `## Unreleased`
  in the feature's own `CHANGELOG.md` (`grimoire/features/auth/CHANGELOG.md`), never in the README:

  ```md
  ## Unreleased

  - 1.0 added described from the existing code
  ```

- **Steps:** take them from the routes and pages, in the order a user meets them. A mail is a
  `*.mail.ts` or `*.email.ts` file (or a file in `mails/` or `emails/`), a job is a queue job or a
  scheduled task. When two sites or apps have a page with one path, write the app after it:
  `page   /support [web-admin]`.
- **Flows:** a flow starts from a route, a page, a job or an event. Logic with no entry point of
  its own (a guard, a calculation) is not a flow: write it in the cases or criteria of the flow
  that reaches it.
- **Cases:** answer the eight questions from what the code does. When the code answers a
  question by doing nothing, that is still what happens: write it as a case with the result
  (`duplicate   saved twice`, `double submit   two accounts`). List a question under
  `## Not handled` only when the behaviour is a gap the owner should decide, in the same form as a
  case (the question, then what happens today):

  ```md
  ## Not handled

  - double submit two quick taps create two accounts
  ```

- **Read-only flows:** a flow that only reads answers the questions that cannot happen with one
  line each, `does not apply: read-only`. That is expected, not a finding.
- **Criteria:** one per case. Tag the existing tests with `@proves` where a test clearly proves
  one. Do not write new tests during a backfill.
- **Intent you cannot see:** write `Unknown: why does a VIP skip the stock check?` in the flow.
  Never invent a reason.

## 4. Describe the apps

One folder per site and mobile app (`describe-an-app`). Declare the conditions you find in the
code (roles, permissions, membership checks). Write page files only for pages that combine
several features or change with the user. When the mobile app defines navigation in code, declare
its screens yourself; they are listed from file names only with file-based routing.

## 5. Check and hand over

```bash
npx warlock grimoire check
```

Fix what it reports about your own files. A backfilled project reports many warnings (criteria with
no test, files with no header); fix errors first and list the warnings for the owner. Then give the owner one list:

- features and flows written, all inferred;
- every `Unknown:` and `Not handled` line, as questions;
- files that belong to no feature;
- files inside a feature that no flow reaches (undescribed behaviour or dead code);
- criteria with no test.

Open one task per question that needs a decision, with `status: waiting for approval` and a
`Decision needed:` line (see `write-a-feature`; any other word is `GR1004`). Mark every task you open
for the owner this way, also when the owner is away. Do not fix code during a backfill; open a task
for each bug you notice.

## Size

Work one feature at a time and finish it before starting the next. A large project takes several
sessions; the task list says where you stopped.


## describe-an-app  `@warlock.js/grimoire/skills/describe-an-app/SKILL.md`

---
name: describe-an-app
description: "Describe where users meet the product in `grimoire/apps/`: one folder per site or mobile app, its named conditions (guest, customer, membership, preferences), shared layouts, and the pages or screens whose blocks point to feature flows. Use when adding a page, a screen or a block, or when what a page shows depends on who is looking."
---

# Describe an app

The Grimoire is experimental: its file structure and commands may still change.

Features say what the product does. Apps say where a user sees it. One folder per site or mobile
app:

```
grimoire/apps/
  web-client/
    README.md              the app and its conditions
    layouts/site.md        blocks every page of this layout shares
    pages/home/README.md   purpose, layout, blocks
    pages/home/blocks/new-arrivals.md   only when the block has page-specific detail
  web-admin/
  mobile/
    screens/home/README.md      declared by you when navigation is in code
```

Write a file only when it says something the code or a feature flow does not already say. A page
with one purpose, no variation and no blocks from other features needs no file.

## The app README

```md
---
id: web-client
type: site
root: src/web/$sites/client
---

# The shop website

## Conditions

- guest not signed in
- customer signed in
- vip customer with the vip membership
- pref:personalised the customer left personalised content on
```

`origin` is optional (`inferred` or `confirmed`), on the README and on layouts, pages and screens,
as on features. Mark files you wrote from the code `inferred`.

Every page and block of this app uses these names and no others in **Who sees it**. Add a condition here before
using it. Name roles and permissions exactly as the access configuration does, so a reader can
find them in the code.

A mobile app in the same repository is one more app: `type: mobile`, `root: mobile`.

## Mobile screens

How a screen gets into the book depends on how the app navigates:

| The mobile app                   | Screens come from                                                  | You write                                                                             |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| File-based routing (Expo Router) | The route file names under its `app` folder (`collectMobileFacts`) | A screen file only when it says something the route does not                          |
| Navigation defined in code       | Nowhere: the book cannot read it                                   | One file per screen you describe, in `grimoire/apps/<app>/screens/<screen>/README.md` |

A declared screen has a `route` (or a `screen` name) in its front matter:

```md
---
screen: order-tracking
---

# Order tracking

## Blocks

| Block         | Flow               | Who sees it | Changes with |
| ------------- | ------------------ | ----------- | ------------ |
| Courier stage | orders/track-order | customer    | —            |
```

When the app uses file-based routing, `warlock grimoire check` reports a screen whose route has no
file. When navigation is in code, declare every screen a flow names; the check cannot verify it.

## A page or screen

```md
---
route: /
layout: site
---

# Home

The first page a visitor sees.

![The home page](../../../../screenshots/web/home.png)

## Blocks

| Block             | Flow                    | Who sees it | Changes with           |
| ----------------- | ----------------------- | ----------- | ---------------------- |
| Featured products | catalog/browse-products | everyone    | vip: member prices     |
| New arrivals      | catalog/new-arrivals    | everyone    | the customer's country |
| Recent orders     | orders/place-order      | customer    | —                      |
```

- **One row per part of the page**, not one description per kind of user. Three roles and two
  preferences are a few rows, not six pages.
- **Flow** is `feature/flow`. The rule for what the block shows lives there. Do not restate it.
- **Who sees it** uses the app's condition names, and the check reports a name the README does
  not declare (`GR5002`). **Changes with** is mostly free text: starting an item
  with a condition name (`vip: member prices`) is checked like Who sees it (`GR5002`), and a name written in backticks
  (`` `vip` ``) that the README does not declare is a warning (`GR5010`). Plain text is never reported, so write
  a condition in backticks only when it is one.
- Do not list blocks that come from the layout.

## A layout

`layouts/site.md` has the same Blocks table for what every page of that layout shares (header,
cart count, notifications bell, footer). Write it once; pages inherit it.

## A block file

Only when the block has something to say about this page in particular:

```md
---
flow: catalog/new-arrivals
---

# New arrivals on the home page

![The new arrivals row](../../../../../screenshots/web/home-new-arrivals.png)

- position second row, under Featured products
- shows a grid of up to 20 products
- phones one row that scrolls sideways
```

## Screenshots

Keep image files in `grimoire/screenshots/` (`.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.webp`, `.gif`), for example
`grimoire/screenshots/web/home.png`. Write an image line `![alt](path)` anywhere in a page, screen
or block file, with the path relative to the Markdown file or starting with `/grimoire/screenshots/`.
The Product map shows these as "where you see it". These are images you attach by hand. The
captures of `@shows` scenes (one per criterion and language) and their approved versions are made by
Warlock under `grimoire/screenshots/captured/` and `approved/`: never write those paths into a page
or block file. An image outside the folder is a warning
(`GR1029`); a missing file is a warning (`GR2014`).

## Where a difference between apps goes

| The difference                                                 | Goes in                             |
| -------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| What the user gets (mobile uses the device location)           | The flow, under `## Differs by app` |
| How it looks or where it sits (a row on mobile, a grid on web) | That app's block file               |

## How a page is reached, and what it requires

Do not write these. The book lists how a page is reached (links and redirects it can read) and
what it requires (middleware and permissions). Write an entry point yourself only when the book
cannot see it, such as a link in an email:

```md
## Also reached from

- mail order-confirmation
```

## Check

```bash
npx warlock grimoire check
```

It reports a block that points to a flow that does not exist, a condition that is not declared in
the app README, a page whose route is gone, a screen with no route (file-based apps), and a
feature that lists an app with no folder here. Its codes are `GR5001` to `GR5010`;
`npx warlock explain GR5003` describes one.


## document-a-file  `@warlock.js/grimoire/skills/document-a-file/SKILL.md`

---
name: document-a-file
description: "Write the one-sentence header and the public-export comments the Grimoire copies into its book, and tag a file with `@feature` when it lives outside its feature's folders. Use whenever you create a source file or change what one is for."
---

# Document a file

The Grimoire is experimental: its file structure and commands may still change.

Warlock copies two things from each source file into the book: the sentence at the top, and the
comment above each public export. They are the only words in the book that you write, and they
are what another agent reads to decide whether to open the file.

## The header: one sentence, first thing in the file

Say why the file exists, from the product's side.

```ts
/** Lists the newest products sold in the customer's country. */

export const NEW_ARRIVALS_LIMIT = 20;
```

- One sentence. If you need two, the file probably does two things.
- Say what it is for, not what kind of file it is. The book already knows it is a service.
- Change it when the file's purpose changes. A stale header misleads every reader after you.

| Write                                      | Not                                  |
| ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------ |
| `Creates a post for the signed-in author.` | `Controller for posts.`              |
| `Sends the order confirmation email.`      | `This file contains the mail class.` |
| `Decides the price a VIP customer pays.`   | `Helper functions.`                  |

## Public exports: one line each

```ts
/** Returns up to 20 products, newest first. */
export async function listNewArrivals(country?: string) {
  // …
}
```

- Comment only what other files import. Private helpers need no comment.
- Say what the caller gets or what happens. Do not repeat the name ("Lists new arrivals").
- Put limits and units in the line when they exist ("up to 20", "in minutes").

## The feature tag: only for exceptions

A file belongs to the feature whose `folders` contain it. Add a tag only when the file lives
somewhere else:

```ts
/**
 * Deletes accounts that were never verified, seven days after sign-up.
 * @feature auth
 */
```

One feature per file. A file used by several features still has one owner; the book lists the
others as borrowing it. Do not tag shared plumbing (config, generic utilities, the base layout).

## Check your work

```bash
npx warlock scry src/app/catalog/services/new-arrivals.service.ts
```

The `about` line and each export's line should read well on their own, without the code beside
them. `npx warlock grimoire check` reports a file with no header and a file with no feature.

## Do not

- Do not write a comment on every function, field or parameter.
- Do not describe the implementation ("uses a loop to…").
- Do not copy the flow's text into the file. The flow lives in `grimoire/features/`.


## guard-a-change  `@warlock.js/grimoire/skills/guard-a-change/SKILL.md`

---
name: guard-a-change
description: "Keep a change inside its task and prove it with `warlock grimoire guard`: files outside the task, deleted proving tests, removed criteria, locked tests, protected areas, the public API snapshot, the code rules and a task id in every commit. Use before you stop work on a task, in CI, and when `GR7006`-`GR7013`, `GR3007`-`GR3010`, `GR4011`, `GR4012` or `GR9008` appear."
---

# Guard a change

The Grimoire is experimental: its file structure and commands may still change.

Agents drift: they remove, change or add things nobody asked for. The guard compares your diff with the task and says what the task did not ask for. Run it before you stop.

```bash
npx warlock grimoire guard            # the one task in progress
npx warlock grimoire guard T-12       # a task by number (T-12, 12 and T-012 match the same task)
npx warlock grimoire guard T-12 --base origin/main
npx warlock grimoire guard --base origin/main --commits origin/main..HEAD   # CI
npx warlock grimoire guard --hook     # agent hook: findings on stderr, exit code 2 on an error
npx warlock grimoire guard --json
```

It never boots the app. The change is the diff from the base (default: where your branch left the default branch) to the working tree, including staged, unstaged and untracked files. Exit code 0 means no error, 1 an error, and with `--hook` 2 (and 0 when it cannot run, such as no task, or when the hook already sent you back once: then finish and list what is left in your report).

## What it checks

| Code               | What                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `GR7006`           | A changed file is outside the task: not owned by its feature (or `Features:`), not a file its flow reaches, not a test proving its criteria, not in `Files:`. |
| `GR7007`           | A flow, criterion or case in `grimoire/features/` is gone and `Removes:` does not name it.                                                                    |
| `GR7008`           | A `@proves` test is gone and no other test proves that criterion, and `Removes:` does not name it.                                                            |
| `GR7009`           | A file in `Locked:` was changed, renamed or deleted.                                                                                                          |
| `GR7010`           | A changed test has fewer assertions than at the base (`expect(`, `expect.soft(`, `assert(`, `assert.x(`, `.should(`; a warning).                              |
| `GR7011`           | A protected area changed and the task's `Touches:` does not name it.                                                                                          |
| `GR7012`           | A commit of `--commits` names no task (`T-12`), or a task that has no file. Merge commits are skipped.                                                        |
| `GR7013`           | `grimoire check` warns when the routes differ from the approved API (the guard raises `GR7011` for `public-api`).                                             |
| `GR3007`-`GR3010`  | The code rules, on the lines the change adds.                                                                                                                 |
| `GR4011`, `GR4012` | An added `.only` or `.skip` (both errors in the guard).                                                                                                       |
| `GR9008`           | No task: pass one, name it in a commit, or have exactly one task `in progress`.                                                                               |
| `GR9009`           | Git could not answer: run in a repository, pass a base that exists, fetch the full history in CI.                                                             |

It also prints the changes that are not approved (`not approved: <n> changes`, from the approved baseline and the screenshots). They do not fail the guard; list them in your report.

## The task body fields

```md
- Files: src/app/shared/utils/money.ts, src/config/catalog.ts
- Features: orders, catalog/wishlist
- Locked: src/app/catalog/tests/wishlist.test.ts
- Touches: migrations, dependencies
- Removes: catalog/wishlist AC-3, catalog/wishlist case duplicate
```

Add a line only when the owner agreed; otherwise change the code. A path with no wildcard matches itself and everything under it; `**` crosses folders, `*` stays inside one.

## Protected areas

`migrations`, `auth`, `config`, `lockfile`, `dependencies` and `public-api` (`DEFAULT_PROTECTED_AREAS`). `dependencies` fires only when a `package.json` adds or changes a dependency entry, not for every edit of the file. `public-api` is the difference between the routes and `grimoire/approved/api.json`; approve a deliberate change with `npx warlock grimoire approve api` (it reads the cached route facts, so run `warlock grimoire build` first). Add or replace areas in `grimoire/settings.md`:

```md
---
protected:
  - payments src/app/payments/** src/config/payments.ts
---
```

## The code rules

`rules:` in `grimoire/settings.md` names the rules `grimoire check` runs on every file (`CODE_RULES`: `logical-css`, `specific-errors`, `type-discriminator`, `no-js-imports`). With no `rules:` key, `check` runs none and the guard runs all four on added lines; `rules: []` turns them off.

| Rule                 | Code     | Flags                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Write instead                                                                                                             |
| -------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `logical-css`        | `GR3007` | `margin-left`, `padding-right`, `left:`, `text-align: left`, `float: right`, `border-left`, Tailwind `ml-4` `pr-2` `left-0` `text-left` `rounded-l-lg` `border-r` (with variants and `-` prefixes), style keys `marginLeft`, `textAlign: "left"` | `margin-inline-start`, `inset-inline-start`, `text-align: start`, `ms-4`, `pe-2`, `start-0`, `text-start`, `rounded-s-lg` |
| `specific-errors`    | `GR3008` | a string that is only "Something went wrong", "An error occurred", "Unknown error", "حدث خطأ ما"…, in code and locale files (`error` and `oops` alone in locale values)                                                                          | say what failed and what to do next, mapped from the error code                                                           |
| `type-discriminator` | `GR3009` | `kind: "a"`, `kind?: "a" \| "b"`                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | `type: "a"`                                                                                                               |
| `no-js-imports`      | `GR3010` | relative `import`/`export … from`/`import()` paths ending `.js`, `.jsx`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`                                                                                                                                                          | `./orders.service`                                                                                                        |

Escape hatch, in a comment on the line or the line above, with a reason: `grimoire-allow logical-css: the code block reads left to right`. Spec files, `node_modules`, `dist` and `grimoire/` are skipped. The scanner reads text, not a syntax tree: JSX text with an apostrophe, regular expressions and your own assertion helpers are read loosely, and editors show no squiggles for these rules.

## When it fails

1. Read each finding: the file and line, then the task it is outside of.
2. Undo what the task did not ask for. Do not edit a locked test, delete a proving test, or add `.skip`.
3. If the file really belongs to the task, add it to `Files:` (or the feature to `Features:`) and say why in the task body, with the owner's agreement.
4. Run the guard again until it prints `guard: ok`.

In CI the scaffold's `.github/workflows/grimoire-guard.yml` runs it on every pull request; the `Stop` hook in `.claude/settings.json` runs `warlock grimoire guard --hook` when an agent finishes.


## record-a-change  `@warlock.js/grimoire/skills/record-a-change/SKILL.md`

---
name: record-a-change
description: "Finish a change the Grimoire way: tie each test to the acceptance criterion it proves, reshape the feature README, add the changelog entry with the right version, move the task to done, run `warlock grimoire check`, and write the release brief. Use after building any change, including a bug fix."
---

# Record a change

The Grimoire is experimental: its file structure and commands may still change.

A change is finished when the code, the tests and the description agree. Do these in order.

## 1. Tie tests to criteria

Put a line above each test that proves a criterion:

```ts
// @proves catalog/new-arrivals AC-2
it("returns the global list when the customer has no country", async () => {
  // …
});
```

A criterion about what a user sees is shown instead, by a browser scene in `e2e/*.e2e.ts`. Put the
comment directly above a `shows()` call that repeats the same criterion:

```ts
import { shows } from "@warlock.js/grimoire/warlock";

// @shows contact/send-message AC-3
await shows(context, "contact/send-message AC-3", async ({ page, language, path }) => {
  await page.mockRequests([{ url: "/api/contact", fail: "unreachable" }]);
  await page.goto(path("/"));
});
```

`shows()` runs the scene once per language and saves a screenshot each (`GRIMOIRE_SHOTS=all`
captures every flow, not only the touched ones). A scene that throws fails that language. The owner
approves the images with `warlock grimoire approve`; list every `GR4017` (image changed), `GR4018`
(flow, criterion, case or proof changed) and `GR4019` (rejected change still there) of the check in
your report, and never edit `grimoire/approved/` yourself. From code, `scanShows` reads the `@shows`
lines of the test files and `resolveSettings` fills the defaults of `grimoire/settings.md`.

- End-to-end tests prove a flow's steps. Unit tests prove a business rule ("a reset code expires
  after 10 minutes").
- One test may prove one criterion. If it needs two tags, split the test.
- A bug fix gets a test that fails without the fix. If no criterion covers the bug, the flow was
  missing a case: add the case and the criterion first.

## 2. Reshape the README and the flow

Edit them so they describe the feature **as it is now**, as if it had always been this way. Do
not append "Update:" notes; history goes in the changelog. Set `updated` to today and `version`
to the new version. Set a flow's `status` to `shipped` once its code and tests exist.

## 3. Add the changelog entry

`grimoire/features/catalog/CHANGELOG.md`, newest first, under `## Unreleased`. Warlock never edits
this file; you write every line of it, including the release number and date when the release ships
(step 6):

```md
## Unreleased

- 2.1 fixed new-arrivals: a customer with no country saw an empty list
  instead of the global one (AC-2)
```

| The change                            | Version                   | Word      |
| ------------------------------------- | ------------------------- | --------- |
| A new flow or a new capability        | next whole number (`3.0`) | `added`   |
| Behaviour of an existing flow changes | next decimal (`2.1`)      | `changed` |
| The code did not match the flow       | next decimal (`2.1`)      | `fixed`   |
| A flow is retired                     | next whole number         | `removed` |

One line per change, written for someone who uses the product. Name the flow, and the criterion
when there is one. While the change is unreleased, write no date and no release number.

## 4. Close the task

Move the file from `grimoire/tasks/open/` to `grimoire/tasks/done/<yyyy-mm>/` and set:

```md
status: done
shipped: catalog 2.1
```

Add two lines: how it was verified (which tests, which criteria) and anything left open. If
something is left open, open a new task for it; do not leave it only in the done file. A task
that needs the owner's answer gets `status: waiting for approval` and a `Decision needed:` line.

Name the task id (`T-12`) in every commit message of the change; `warlock grimoire guard --commits <range>` fails a commit that names none.

## 5. Check

```bash
npx warlock grimoire check
```

| It reports                                                          | Do                                                    |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| A step names a route, page, mail or job that does not exist         | Fix the name in the flow, or the code                 |
| A criterion has no test                                             | Write the test, or say in the task why not            |
| A test points at a criterion that does not exist                    | Fix the `@proves` line                                |
| Proofs exist but no test results were found (`GR4009`)              | Record results, see below                             |
| A proving test the reporter could not match (`GR4010`)              | Fix the `@proves` line or the test name               |
| A file has no header, or no feature                                 | `document-a-file`                                     |
| A file in the feature's folders that no flow reaches                | Describe the behaviour in a flow, or delete dead code |
| A README `updated` older than its newest changelog entry            | Reshape the README                                    |
| A changelog version that does not fit the word (`added` with `2.1`) | Fix the version                                       |

Migrations, seeds, commands, the main file, layouts, roots and test helpers only specs import are never reported (`GR3006`); a route step reaches the middleware its route names. Do not try to describe those in a flow.

**Recording results.** The check and the devtools tab read test results from
`grimoire/book/test-results.json`, written by the Grimoire Vitest reporter when the tests run. That
folder is not committed, so run the tests with the reporter in CI and ship the results file with the
deploy. To write it elsewhere, pass `grimoireReporter({ file })` and point the devtools panel at it
with the `testResultsFile` option.

Then check the change against its task, before you stop:

```bash
npx warlock grimoire guard T-12
```

It lists files outside the task, deleted proving tests, removed criteria or cases, edited locked tests, protected areas the task does not name, and the code rules on the lines you added. Fix the code rather than widening the task; add a `Files:`, `Touches:` or `Removes:` line only when the owner agreed (`guard-a-change`).

Fix every line it prints. Do not finish with problems you caused. Findings on a flow or feature
with `status: proposed` print with `(expected)` and do not fail the check: leave them until the
code exists.

## 6. At release time

Run the stamp from the app's release flow, after the version is set in `package.json`:

```bash
npx warlock grimoire release --stamp
```

It does three things, in this order, and prints what it did (`stamped catalog, orders → 1.4.1 (2026-11-20)`):

1. **Stamps the changelogs.** In each feature that has entries under `## Unreleased`, it moves them under a
   heading with the release number and date, and leaves an empty `## Unreleased` above:

   ```md
   ## Unreleased

   ## 1.4.1 (2026-11-20)

   - 2.1 fixed new-arrivals: a customer with no country saw an empty list
     instead of the global one (AC-2)
   ```

2. **Writes the release file** `grimoire/releases/1.4.1.md` when it is missing, with its front matter, a
   `# Release 1.4.1` heading and a one-line brief that names the changed features. An existing release file is kept.
   **Rewrite the brief in the owner's words**: two or three sentences on what the release means to users.

   ```md
   ---
   release: 1.4.1
   date: 2026-11-20
   ---

   # Release 1.4.1

   Customers with no country on their account see new arrivals again.
   ```

3. **Collects the list** between the markers under your brief. Run `npx warlock grimoire release 1.4.1` again after
   any change to a changelog or the brief: the result is the same every time. It also says how many entries are
   still unreleased. Do not write that list yourself.

The version is the app's `package.json` version unless you pass one (`release 1.4.1 --stamp`); the date is today unless
the release file has one or you pass `--date yyyy-mm-dd`. The stamp is the only edit Warlock makes to your files, and
only with `--stamp`. Without it you move the entries and write the release file by hand, as above, and run
`npx warlock grimoire release 1.4.1`.

`npx warlock grimoire check` reports a listed entry that has no changelog entry stamped with that
release and date, and a release section with no release file.

## Report to the owner

Say what changed in plain words, the feature version, which criteria are proven, what the check
reported, and what is left open with its task id. Paste the result of `npx warlock grimoire guard`,
and list every change that is not approved (`warlock grimoire check` `GR4017`, `GR4018`, `GR4019`) by
its id; leave none out.


## review-a-change  `@warlock.js/grimoire/skills/review-a-change/SKILL.md`

---
name: review-a-change
description: "Review a change as an independent reviewer who sees only the task and the diff, never the author's summary, and answers one question: list every change the task did not ask for. Use when asked to review work an agent or a colleague finished, before a merge."
---

# Review a change

The Grimoire is experimental: its file structure and commands may still change.

The reviewer is independent. It reads two things only: the task file and the diff. It does not read the author's summary, the commit messages' explanations or the author's report; they describe what the author meant, not what changed.

## Input

1. The task file (`grimoire/tasks/open/T-12-….md` or `grimoire/tasks/done/…`), including its `Files:`, `Features:`, `Locked:`, `Touches:` and `Removes:` lines.
2. The diff: `git diff <base>...HEAD`, where `<base>` is the branch the change merges into (`origin/main`).

## The question

Ask exactly this, and answer it before anything else:

> List every change the task did not ask for.

Go file by file through the diff. For each hunk say which sentence or acceptance criterion of the task asks for it. A hunk no sentence asks for goes on the list: an unasked file, a removed or reworded criterion, a deleted or weakened test, a renamed export, a changed dependency, a new behaviour, a refactor. "Harmless" and "an improvement" are not reasons to leave it out.

## Then

1. Run the guard and paste its output:

   ```bash
   npx warlock grimoire guard <task> --base <base>
   ```

2. List every drift item that is not approved, by id, from `npx warlock grimoire check` (`GR4017` capture differs, `GR4018` structure changed, `GR4019` rejected change still there). Leave none out and do not approve any: only the owner approves.
3. Say whether the change is ready: yes only when the list of unasked changes is empty (or each item is named in the task and approved by the owner), the guard prints `guard: ok`, and no drift item is open.

## Report shape

```md
Unasked changes

- <file>: <what changed>, no sentence of the task asks for it

Guard
<the pasted output>

Not approved

- <drift item id>

Verdict: ready | not ready, because …
```

An empty "Unasked changes" section says "none" and the reviewer says which files it read.


## use-the-grimoire  `@warlock.js/grimoire/skills/use-the-grimoire/SKILL.md`

---
name: use-the-grimoire
description: "Find the right files before changing a Warlock.js project by asking the Grimoire (experimental): `warlock scry` for a file, a route, a feature, a flow or the impact of a change, and the `grimoire/` folder for what the product does. Use at the start of every task, before searching the code."
---

# Use the Grimoire

The Grimoire is experimental: its file structure and commands may still change.

`grimoire/` is the map of this project. Read it before you search the code: it tells you where
things are, what a feature is meant to do, and what a change will touch.

| Folder               | Holds                                                   | Written by                                     |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `grimoire/book/`     | One entry per source file, plus routes and pages        | Warlock (never edit)                           |
| `grimoire/features/` | What the product does: features, flows, cases, criteria | You and other agents                           |
| `grimoire/apps/`     | Where users meet it: sites, mobile apps, pages, blocks  | You and other agents                           |
| `grimoire/tasks/`    | Open and finished work                                  | You and other agents                           |
| `grimoire/releases/` | What each release shipped                               | You write the brief, Warlock collects the list |

Files named `index.json`, `bookmap.json` or ending in `.bookmap.json` are Warlock's. A feature's
`bookmap.json` says what the feature owns and borrows, and each flow's `*.bookmap.json` says which
files sit behind each step and which tests prove each criterion. They are rebuilt on demand and are
not in git. Never edit them; change the code or the written files and they follow. Warlock never
edits a file you wrote either.

## Start of every task

1. `scry --search "<the whole request>"`: pass the whole task sentence (the commit title or the bug report), not two keywords.

   ```bash
   npx warlock scry --search "new arrivals are empty for customers with no country"
   ```

   ```text
   21.4  flow     catalog/new-arrivals              New arrivals
    9.8  file     src/app/catalog/services/new-arrivals.service.ts  Lists the newest products sold in the customer's country.
   changes with the top hits:
     src/app/catalog/repositories/products.repository.ts   imported by new-arrivals.service.ts
     src/app/catalog/tests/new-arrivals.test.ts            test
   next: warlock scry --impact src/app/catalog/services/new-arrivals.service.ts
   ```

   The number in front is the score: hits are in score order, best first, whatever the type.

2. `scry --impact <top file>` (the `next:` line) and read the `changes with` lines: they are the files that usually change
   with it (what it imports and what imports it inside the same feature, and its tests).
3. Use grep only for literal text, or when the answer says `weak match`.
4. Read the feature's `README.md`, then the flow file. They say what the behaviour should be.
5. Ask for the flow's book map. It lists the files behind each step, the tests that prove each
   criterion and the pages that show the flow.

   ```bash
   npx warlock scry --flow catalog/new-arrivals
   ```

6. Read only those files. Do not read a whole module to find one function.

## Questions the book answers

```bash
npx warlock scry src/app/catalog/services/new-arrivals.service.ts   # what is this file?
npx warlock scry --impact src/app/catalog/models/product.model.ts   # what breaks if I change it?
npx warlock scry --route "POST /api/orders"                         # what is behind this URL?
npx warlock scry --route "GET /chat"                                # a page URL works too (--site <id> picks one site)
npx warlock scry --feature catalog                                  # the whole feature
npx warlock scry --flow catalog/new-arrivals                        # one flow, step by step
```

`scry` only reads the book the last `warlock grimoire build` left; it never rebuilds it. After you
finish editing files, run `npx warlock grimoire build`. When code, test or written files differ from
the book, the answer is the stored one and ends with
`note book is stale (12 files changed); run warlock grimoire build` (in `--json`, the `notes` list):
build, then ask again. A project with no book stops with `GR9007`. A note
`route facts look incomplete; run warlock grimoire build` means the stored routes are missing their source files
(an empty or partial route list): `--route` and `--impact` routes cannot be trusted until you build.

Add `--json` for machine-readable output; a failed call then prints `{ "type": "error", "code", "message", "fix" }` on stdout and exits 1 (the scry MCP tools return the same JSON as their error text). `--impact` lists API routes, pages, flows and features,
including features that only borrow the file; each list has a count and stops at 20 lines, and `--all`
prints every line. `--search` takes the whole sentence (the commit title or the bug report, not two keywords): hits whose name or title holds the words come first, every other hit follows by score, and the list is printed in score order with the score in front. It also reads a flow's summary, story, cases and criteria (`AC-5` works); a hit found by written text shows the part that matched in brackets. Page, screen, block and file hits carry their app, and `--app <id>` keeps one app's hits. Specs, locale files and type files rank below code of an equal match. Search reads Arabic and accented Latin text too: accents, Arabic vowel marks, hamza forms and the leading article `ال` do not matter (`شحنة` finds `الشحنة`, `cafe` finds `café`). The answer's `alsoChanges` list (`changes with the top hits:`, at most 10 files) and `next` line come from the top three hits; `weak: true` (the line `weak match: …`) says no hit holds most of the request's words. Read the flows it names and run their tests after
your change.

A file's entry is also at a fixed path: `src/app/auth/controllers/login.controller.ts` is described
in `grimoire/book/app/auth/controllers/login.controller.json`.

## Commands

| Command                                     | Does                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `warlock grimoire build`                    | Builds or refreshes the book (and its derived data). Run it after you finish editing; `scry` only reads and never builds                 |
| `warlock grimoire build --site [--out dir]` | Also writes the book as a static site (default `grimoire/book/site`); skipped when the folder is already current (`--force` writes it)   |
| `warlock grimoire build --site --product`   | Writes the business export: the Product map only, no file paths, test names or per-file answers                                          |
| `warlock grimoire check`                    | Reports broken names, untested criteria, files with no owner. Exit 1 on an error; `--all` lists every warning                            |
| `warlock grimoire release <release>`        | Writes the collected list into `grimoire/releases/<release>.md`; with `--stamp` it first moves `## Unreleased` entries under the version |
| `warlock explain GR2001`                    | Explains a finding code                                                                                                                  |

Every finding has a code (`GR2001`) and a fix hint. A finding marked `(expected)` belongs to work
that is still `proposed`; it does not fail the check.

## What to trust

- **Exports, imports, importers, routes, middleware, pages:** read from the code. Trust them.
- **Route middleware:** a route step also reaches the middleware files the matched route names (not the routes file's other imports). Roles that run by being present (migration, seed, command, main, layout, root) and spec-only helpers are not listed as unreached.
- **Dev tab route facts:** the dev tab reads routes, events and jobs from the running dev server (nothing is booted twice), so it shows `routes: fresh` on the first open, and reads them again after a routes file changes. `scry` and the MCP tools use the routes of the last `warlock grimoire build`.
- **Without route facts** (`routes: missing`): route, mail, notification, job and event steps are `found: null` (not checked), not resolved and not failed; `GR5008` skips mail and notification entries.
- **Files behind a route:** every file the handler can reach through imports. It is not the exact
  call path; open the handler to see which ones it really uses.
- **Reached from:** only links and redirects written as plain values. `unknown` means look.
- **Written files:** they say what should happen. When the code disagrees with a flow, do not
  pick one silently. Say which is wrong, and fix it or ask the owner.

## When there is nothing to find

- No flow matches the task: the behaviour is undescribed. Describe it first with
  `write-a-feature`, then change the code.
- The command says the book is missing (`GR9007`) or stale (`note book is stale …`): run
  `npx warlock grimoire build`, then ask again. If the build reports problems, read them;
  `npx warlock grimoire check` prints the same list.
- The project has code but no `grimoire/` folder: use `backfill-a-grimoire`.

## See also

`write-a-feature`, `record-a-change`, `describe-an-app`, `document-a-file`, `backfill-a-grimoire`.

## From code

The same answers are available as functions, for tools that build on the Grimoire.

From `@warlock.js/grimoire` (no dependency on core or web):

- `openGrimoire` loads everything once (it runs `parseGrimoire`, `buildBook`, `matchApps`,
  `resolveOwnership`, `scanProofs`, `readTestResults`, `buildCollectedFiles`, then `writeBook`
  and `writeCollectedFiles`), and returns a snapshot.
- `openStoredGrimoire(root, adapter)` is the read-only open behind `scry` (the stored snapshot, `behind` set when files moved; `GR9007` when never built) and `checkBook()` is `buildBook`'s change check with nothing rebuilt or written.
- `scry` answers a query from the snapshot; `formatScryResult` prints it; `parseScryQuery` reads
  CLI arguments into a query. `SCRY_STOP_WORDS` is the set of small words search leaves out (add to it
  before the first search of a process).
- `checkGrimoire` runs every rule; `formatCheckReport` prints the report. Each finding has a code
  from `GRIMOIRE_CODES` (also `GRIMOIRE_CODE_LIST`); `explainGrimoireCode`, `isGrimoireCode` and
  `grimoireCodeDocsUrl` (based on `GRIMOIRE_CODES_DOCS_URL`) describe it, and rules build
  findings with `createFinding`. Commands throw `GrimoireError` with a code.
- `collectRelease`, `renderCollectedList` and `writeRelease` gather the changelog entries of a
  release between `COLLECTED_START_MARKER` and `COLLECTED_END_MARKER`.
- `scanProofs` and `scanProofsInText` read `// @proves` lines; `criterionStatus` turns test
  results into a criterion's status; `CASE_QUESTIONS` lists the questions every flow answers.
- Flow steps list `entries` (every file the step starts from), `direct` (their direct imports), `files` (what
  runs: type-only imports are not followed) and `typeOnlyFiles` (reached only through type-only imports).
  `importClosure(graph, start, { skipTypeOnly: true })` leaves type-only edges out. `warlock scry --flow --json`
  keeps every list; the MCP tool `grimoire_flow` and the devtools flow route send counts and the first 50 direct
  imports per step, and list one step's files on request (`files: "reachable"` or `"type-only"` with `step`).
- Helpers: `loadBook`, `readFrontMatter`, `fileGraph`, `importClosure`, `importerClosure`,
  `bookEntryPath`, `bookEntryPaths`, `toPosixPath`, `GRIMOIRE_DIR`, `GRIMOIRE_PATHS`,
  `GRIMOIRE_IGNORE_RULES` (the `.gitignore` lines) and `BOOK_SCHEMA_VERSION`.

From `@warlock.js/grimoire/warlock` (needs `@warlock.js/core`): `registerGrimoireCommands` returns
the `grimoire` and `scry` commands for `cli.commands` in `warlock.config.ts`;
`createWarlockAdapter` builds the adapter that feeds the book from the inspect report (it also supplies the
optional `host()` described below);
`collectMobileFacts` lists mobile screens from Expo Router file names.

A custom `BookAdapter` may add `host(root)`, returning `{ name, version, logo, app }` (the framework's name,
installed version and a small `data:` logo, and the app's own `{ name, version }`), or `null`. The tab shows the
framework logo and version in its header and the app name and version at the bottom, in the static export and
in the shared Product map too; an adapter without `host()` shows nothing. The summary and product answers carry it
as `host` (`null` when absent); the feature answer's `flows` also carry `steps`, `cases`, `criteria`, `tested` and
`findings` counts.

The devtools feature route (`/features/:feature`) adds three fields for the tabbed page: `map` (the feature map:
`columns` are each site and mobile app the flows touch, titled by the app's heading, then `api`, then `background`;
`rows` has one entry per flow with `cells` keyed by column id, each cell a list of chips `{ step, type, label, found,
app, page, method, path, file }` taken from the steps the book already resolved), `fileGroups` (the own files by module)
and `proofs` (each flow's criteria with their tests). Each product map feature card carries `strip`: `flows`
`{ total, shipped }`, `criteria` `{ total, proven, failing, measured }` (`measured` is `false` when tagged tests have no
recorded results), `screenshots` `{ places, present }` and `findings` `{ errors, warnings }`. The feature and flow pages
have tabs with their own hash routes: `feature/<id>[/flows|files|findings|tests]` and
`flow/<feature>/<flow>[/proof|files|findings]`.

From `@warlock.js/grimoire/vitest`: `grimoireReporter` records the last result of every test marked
`// @proves` into `grimoire/book/test-results.json`. Add it to the Vitest `reporters` list.
`grimoireReporter({ file })` writes to another path (for a deploy that ships CI results); `readTestResults(root, file?)`
reads it, and the panel option `testResultsFile` and `openGrimoire` option `testResultsFile` point the tab at it.
The check warns with `GR4009` when `@proves` lines exist and no results were found, and with `GR4010` when the
reporter could not match a proving test.

From `@warlock.js/grimoire/devtools`: `grimoireDevtoolsPanel` (the default export) is the Grimoire
tab for `@warlock.js/devtools`, listed in `panels` of `src/config/devtools.ts`;
`exportGrimoireSite` writes the same view as a static site.
The tab keeps its snapshot until the book changes in production and refreshes it in the background in
development; the results file's modified time is part of the change stamp, so new results show without a restart.
The tab also has a Product map: the features, flows, apps, releases and planned work in plain words, from the written
files (summaries, `audience`, `## Why`, `## Story`) and the images in `grimoire/screenshots/`. Its routes are
`/product`, `/product/features/:feature` and `/product/flows/:feature/:flow`; `/check/groups` and `/check?code=`
give the check by code and a page of one code's findings. Set `ttlMs` with `panels: [["@warlock.js/grimoire/devtools", { ttlMs: 60_000 }]]`.


## write-a-feature  `@warlock.js/grimoire/skills/write-a-feature/SKILL.md`

---
name: write-a-feature
description: "Describe a new feature, or a new version of one, in `grimoire/features/` before writing code: the task, the brief, the README front matter, each flow with its steps, cases and acceptance criteria. Use when the owner asks for something the product does not do yet."
---

# Write a feature

The Grimoire is experimental: its file structure and commands may still change.

Describe the behaviour first, then build it. The description is the brief the owner approves and
the thing your tests will prove.

## Is it a feature, a flow, or a change?

- **A feature** is something a user or another system can do, named from their side (`auth`,
  `catalog`, `orders`). It has roughly two to ten flows.
- **A flow** is one path through it (`sign-up`, `google-login`, `new-arrivals`).
- **A new capability** in an existing feature is a new whole-number version (`2.0`) with its
  own brief. **A small change or a fix** is a decimal (`2.1`) and needs no brief: go to
  `record-a-change`.
- A notification, mail or job belongs to the feature whose business reason creates it. "Your
  order shipped" belongs to `orders`, not to `notifications`.

## 1. Open a task

`grimoire/tasks/open/T-014-wishlist.md`:

```md
---
id: T-014
type: feature
feature: catalog
apps: [web-client, mobile]
status: waiting for approval
---

# Let customers save products to a wishlist

- Asked by: the owner, 2026-11-16
- Why: customers ask to keep products for later
- Brief: features/catalog/versions/v3.md
- Decision needed: one wishlist per customer, or several named lists?
```

The guard (`warlock grimoire guard`, see `guard-a-change`) reads these optional body lines, comma-separated:

```md
- Files: src/app/shared/utils/money.ts, src/config/catalog.ts
- Features: orders, catalog/wishlist
- Locked: src/app/catalog/tests/wishlist.test.ts
- Touches: migrations, dependencies
- Removes: catalog/wishlist AC-3, catalog/wishlist case duplicate
```

- `Files:` lists files (globs allowed) outside the task's feature that the change must touch.
- `Features:` names more features (`orders`) or flows (`catalog/wishlist`) the change may touch.
- `Locked:` names the acceptance tests the planner wrote first. Whoever builds the task never edits them.
- `Touches:` names the protected areas the task may change: `migrations`, `auth`, `config`, `lockfile`, `dependencies`, `public-api`, or an area of `grimoire/settings.md`.
- `Removes:` names the flow, criterion or case that is allowed to go (`<feature>/<flow>`, `<feature>/<flow> AC-3`, `<feature>/<flow> case duplicate`).

Write the acceptance tests first, with their `@proves` lines, and list them in `Locked:` before handing the task to an implementer. The task's `feature` and `flow` already put that feature's files and the flow's files in scope; add `Files:` for the rest at the start, not after the guard fails.

A task that waits for the owner's answer has `status: waiting for approval` and a `Decision needed:` line.
The other statuses are `open`, `approved`, `in progress`, `blocked`, `done` and `dropped`; any other
word is an error (`GR1004`).

## 2. Write the brief

`grimoire/features/catalog/versions/v3.md`: why, what changes (which flows are new or changed),
and what is out of scope. Keep it to one screen.

## Write `design-system` first

In a project that has a UI, create the `design-system` feature before any other. Its flows are the
rules every screen follows: `direction` (inputs and text follow the reading direction, a page is
mirrored in Arabic), `components` (every component renders in each language), `error-messages`
(every error says what failed and what to do next), plus spacing and colours (contrast) when the
project has rules for them. Every flow with a `page` step names `design-system` under
`## Affects and affected by` (`- affects design-system`), so a change to a screen is checked against it.
Its criteria are shown with `@shows` scenes (`record-a-change`).

## 3. Write or update the feature README

```md
---
id: catalog
title: Product catalog
status: proposed
version: 3.0
updated: 2026-11-16
apps: [web-client, mobile]
folders: [src/app/catalog, src/web/$sites/client/products]
audience: [shoppers, store staff]
---

# Product catalog

Customers browse products, search them and see what is new.

## Why

Shoppers decide what to buy from the catalog, so it has to be quick to browse and clear about what is new.

## Flows

- browse-products list and filter products
- new-arrivals the newest products sold in the customer's country
- wishlist save a product for later

## Affects and affected by

- affected by orders/place-order (lowers stock)
```

`audience` (optional) lists who the feature is for, in plain words. `## Why` (optional) says why the
feature exists in a few sentences. Without `audience`, readers use the `who` of the flows.

`id` never changes. `folders` are the folders whose files belong to this feature. An entry with a
code-file extension names one file (`src/web/components/client/home/pricing-table.tsx`), for a
feature that owns a few files in a folder shared with others. A file entry wins over the folder
of another feature; each file has one owner. `apps` must
exist under `grimoire/apps/`. A feature whose folders hold no file yet is fine while it is
`proposed`.

## 4. Write each flow

`grimoire/features/catalog/flows/wishlist.md`:

```md
---
id: wishlist
since: 3.0
status: proposed
who: customer
---

# Save a product to the wishlist

A customer saves a product they like and finds it again later on their wishlist.

## Story

1. The customer opens a product and taps "Save for later".
2. The product shows a filled heart.
   ![The saved product](../../../screenshots/web/wishlist-saved.png)
3. Later, the customer opens their wishlist and sees the product there.

## Steps

1. page /products/:id
2. route POST /wishlist
3. notification wishlist-price-drop
4. page /wishlist

## Differs by app

- mobile the save button is also on the product card in lists

## Cases

- invalid input a product id that is not an id → 422
- not allowed guest → sent to sign in, then back to the product
- not found the product does not exist → 404
- duplicate already saved → stays saved, no error (AC-2)
- limits at most 200 products
- expiry does not apply: saved products do not expire
- double submit two taps save once
- outside service down does not apply: no outside service is called
- server unreachable the save button shows "Could not reach the server, check your connection" (AC-5)
- server error the product stays unsaved and the message says what failed (AC-5)

## Acceptance criteria

- AC-1 a saved product appears on /wishlist
- AC-2 saving twice keeps one entry
- AC-3 a guest is sent to sign in and returns to the product
- AC-4 [mobile] the product card has a save button
- AC-5 a failed save says what failed and what to do next
```

**Summary.** The paragraph under the `# Title`: one or two plain sentences saying who does what and
what they get. A flow with none gets a warning (`GR1030`).

**Story.** Optional. Numbered sentences in the user's words, without file names or code, for readers
who do not read code. Indent a second line to continue a sentence. An image line
`![alt](path)` under a step attaches a screenshot to it.

**Screenshots.** Keep image files in `grimoire/screenshots/` (any subfolders; `.png`, `.jpg`,
`.jpeg`, `.webp` or `.gif`). Write the path relative to the Markdown file, so it also shows on a git
host (`../../../screenshots/web/wishlist-saved.png` from a flow file), or start it with
`/grimoire/screenshots/`. An image outside that folder is a warning (`GR1029`), a missing file too
(`GR2014`).

**Product map.** The Grimoire tab has a Product map for readers who are not developers. They see the
flow summary, the feature's why and audience, the story in plain words and the screenshots there,
so write them for a person who has never opened the code.

**Steps.** Each step has a kind and the name used in code: `page`, `route`, `mail`,
`notification`, `job`, `event`, `outside service`. Use `affects` for an effect on another
feature (`affects   catalog/stock`). Warlock checks every name exists. A mail is a `*.mail.ts` or
`*.email.ts` file, or a file in a `mails/` or `emails/` folder; a job is a queue job
(`defineJob()`) or a scheduled task, by its name in code.

When two sites, or a site and the mobile app, have a page with the same path, name the app after
the path in brackets: `page   /support [web-admin]`. The step then looks in that app only (its
pages, or its screens for a mobile app). Without brackets it looks in the apps the feature lists.

**Screenshots of a flow.** Criteria about what a user sees are shown in each language of the app
(`languages` in `grimoire/settings.md`), so one criterion gives one screenshot per language. Write a
criterion once; do not write one per language. A flow with nothing to look at (no screen, or a
screen that cannot be captured) says `screenshots: false` in its front matter. `screenshots` is
`false` or absent; the modes `changed`, `all` and `off` live in the settings
(`SCREENSHOT_MODES`, default `DEFAULT_GRIMOIRE_SETTINGS.screenshots`, `changed`).

**Cases.** End a case line with `(AC-n)` (or `(AC-1, AC-2)`) to link it to the criterion that
proves it; a number the flow does not have is an error (`GR2013`). Answer all eight questions (invalid input, not allowed, not found, duplicate, limits,
expiry, double submit, outside service down), each with a case or "does not apply" and the
reason. A flow with a `page` step also answers the two UI questions (`UI_CASE_QUESTIONS`):
`server unreachable` (what the user sees when the request never arrives) and `server error`
(when the server answers with a failure); the screen of each is shown with a scene that mocks
the request. A flow that skips one gets a finding, except that a flow with no writes (only pages and
`GET` routes) may leave out `duplicate` and `double submit`. Do not invent cases beyond the questions unless the owner described one.

**Criteria.** One per case that changes what the user gets. Number them `AC-1`, `AC-2`, … and
never renumber. Scope one to an app with `[app-id]`.

**App differences.** What the user gets differs → here, under the app's name. How it looks or
where it sits → the app's block file (`describe-an-app`).

## 5. Stop for approval

For a new feature or a whole-number version, stop here. Tell the owner the task id and the brief
path, list the decisions you need, and wait. Do not write code first.

## 6. Check

```bash
npx warlock grimoire check
```

Until the code exists it reports the routes and pages you named as missing. Findings on a flow or
feature with `status: proposed` print with `(expected)` and do not fail the check; everything else
it reports must be fixed.

Then build, and follow `record-a-change`.
